name: Tecan Group AG
subcategory: laboratory automation and liquid handling (Freedom EVO, Fluent), OEM instrument components and contract manufacturing (closed comparator)
origin_detail: Founded on 18 March 1980 by engineers Heinz Abplanalp, Heini Maurer, Heinz Möckli and Gallus Blater, first in Abplanalp's home in Hombrechtikon; the name stands for 'Technische Analysegeräte'. Perkin-Elmer held the majority of voting shares from 1997 and sold out in 1999, when Tecan relisted in the main segment of the SWX Swiss Exchange (SIX: TECN). HQ Männedorf, canton of Zürich.
flagship_projects: Fluent laboratory automation (2014-2015) and FluentControl software
openness_notes: Instruments, firmware and control software (EVOware, FluentControl) are proprietary; no open-source releases or published design files were found on fetched Tecan pages, whose history page does not mention open interfaces or APIs. Third parties have opened the interface instead: the community PyLabRobot SDK (MIT) can drive a Tecan EVO, and its site does not list Tecan among its vendor supporters. Level 0 on the hardware scale throughout.

license_history.note: Closed instruments and software throughout; no relicensing found

exit_events.note: Second listing, in the main segment, after Perkin-Elmer sold its majority stake on the open market; Wikipedia does not give the original listing year

risk_events: 1989: financial difficulties led to a temporary suspension of share trading; 1990 restructuring sold many subsidiaries to focus on laboratory automation
2021: COVID-era peak; sales grew 29.5% to CHF 946.6M and Tecan made its largest acquisition ever (Paramit, US contract manufacturer, completed August 2021; price not found on fetched pages)
2022-2025: sales fell from CHF 1.14B (2022) to CHF 882.5M (2025), with declines of 6.1%, 13.0% and 5.5% in 2023-2025; trailing 12 months to June 2026 CHF 870.5M (-4.0%)
Market cap fell from CHF 7.04B (end-2021) to CHF 1.63B (end-2025), about -77%, before recovering to CHF 3.03B on 2026-11-23
robustness: A 46-year-old listed incumbent with ~3,500 staff in 52 countries and a diversified mix of own-brand automation, OEM components (Cavro) and contract manufacturing (Paramit). Its closed platforms tie customers to Tecan software and consumables; community drivers (PyLabRobot) give users a partial exit for the EVO but are unsupported by Tecan.
physical_science_relevance: Tecan liquid handlers are built for life-science and diagnostics labs, but the same pipetting robots are used to prepare precursor solutions in chemistry and materials automation. For a self-driving lab, a Tecan EVO can be scripted from open Python via PyLabRobot rather than only through EVOware. Little direct relevance to LPBF alloy development, which is powder- and furnace-based rather than liquid-based.
openness_effect_assessment: Tecan shows that a fully closed instrument incumbent can last decades and grow by acquisition: no openness was needed for its 1990s-2021 expansion. Its recent stress came from the end of pandemic demand (sales -23% from 2022 to 2025, market cap -77% from end-2021 to end-2025), not from open competitors. Openness reaches its machines only from outside, through community drivers such as PyLabRobot.
key_takeaway: Tecan is the archetypal closed liquid-handling incumbent: founded by four engineers in 1980, listed since 1999 and built on proprietary Genesis, Freedom EVO and Fluent platforms plus OEM manufacturing. Its 2021 COVID peak and largest-ever acquisition were followed by four years of falling sales and a 77% fall in market value to end-2025. For an open lab, Tecan robots are usable mainly through community open-source drivers that Tecan does not sponsor.
